entries.title: Jeremiah 41:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Now - Three months after the city was taken. Ishmael - The same Ishmael that came to Gedaliah, ver. 8 ,9, to whom he sware protection; only here we are told he was of the royal blood, which might both raise his spirits, as having a more legal pretence to the government, and rendered him a fitter instrument, for Baalis the king or queen of the Ammonites to make use of. The princes - Some of the princes, who had escaped the army of the king of Babylon.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Slew - All those who were about the court of Gedaliah.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No man - No man who lived at any distance from Mizpah.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: There came men - Who possibly had not heard of the temple being burnt. Cut themselves - With all indications of mourning used in those countries.

entries.title: Jeremiah 41:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He forebare - His covetousness prevailed over his cruelty.
